title: German Hyperinflation of 1923
summary: During 1923 the German Mark lost value so fast that wages were paid daily and people rushed to spend notes at once. The government ended the crisis with a currency reform: the Deutsche Rentenbank was founded in October and began issuing Rentenmark notes in mid-November 1923, replacing the Mark after savings and debts had nearly vanished.

uncertainty.note: Bundesbank frames the inflation as 1914-23; this record covers the hyperinflation phase of 1923 ending with the Rentenmark.

where.modern_name: Berlin, Germany (proxy pin for a nationwide event)
where.historical_name: Berlin, Weimar Republic (German Reich); pin is a proxy, the event affected all Germany

importance.justification: Collapse of the German currency in 1923 and its reform shaped Weimar Germany and later views of inflation.

sources.title: Vor 100 Jahren: Die Hyperinflation von 1923 - Von der Rentenmark zur Förderbank

reviewer_note: Pin is a Berlin proxy for a Germany-wide event. Both sources are German public institutions; Rentenbank is the successor-linked development bank, so not fully neutral. Exact 15 November issue date not confirmed.
